scope: Reviewed OMAI formula endpoints and exact Lean proof source for local theorems with no Physlib physics counterpart. Hash and compiled-name checks detect drift and provenance errors; they are not automatic symbolic translation or numerical validation.
interpretations: compute_carrier_mobility is an opaque amset output in the catalog. The interpreted definition is the Boltzmann mobility mu = c sum_k w_k tau_k of one diagonal component for one carrier type, with c = e/n > 0, w_k >= 0 the Fermi-window and squared-velocity weights of the states k, and the state relaxation time tau_k = (sum_i 1/tau_{k,i})^-1 obtained by adding the mechanism rates in every state; mu_i = c sum_k w_k tau_{k,i} is the mobility of mechanism i alone, which amset reports with separate_mobility.

With c > 0, w_k >= 0 and every tau_{k,i} > 0, mu <= (sum_i 1/mu_i)^-1: Matthiessen's rule on the mechanism-resolved mobilities never underestimates the mobility. Equality and the size of the gap are not characterized.

compute_electronic_dos is an opaque Kohn-Sham output in the catalog. The interpreted definition is the density of states sum_b g_b delta(E - E_b) of a finite set of levels E_b with degeneracies g_b > 0 (spin and k-point weights), read as its integral sum_b g_b phi(E_b) against a test function phi; the smeared or tetrahedron histogram of the codes is not covered.

At k_B T > 0 the electron count N(mu) = sum_b g_b/(1 + exp((E_b - mu)/(k_B T))), the density of states integrated against the Fermi function, is continuous and strictly increasing in mu from 0 to sum_b g_b, so every count strictly between those limits fixes exactly one chemical potential. At T = 0 the Fermi level of a gapped level set is not unique.
